CREMAWORKS · NEW MANAGER ORIENTATION

Your factory. Your decisions. Your reputation.

CremaWorks makes premium espresso machines for specialty cafés and serious home baristas. Sales is growing—but forecasts, component shortages, and production schedules are no longer keeping pace.

You've just been hired as Production Planning Manager. Your assignment is to turn demand into a workable manufacturing plan and get finished machines ready for customers.

🚚 DeliveryCover customer requirements.
📦 InventoryAvoid unnecessary stock.
🏭 ProductionKeep components and assembly aligned.

Your command center: SAP-style MD04. You'll enter PIRs, run multilevel MRP, investigate the BOM, and execute production. Five missions, 500 points, and the full procurement document chain.

Event log

Bill of materials (BOM)

Select a material to view its MD04. Shared components receive dependent requirements from BOTH parent assemblies.
Run MRP to explode all three BOM levels.

Multilevel MRP: Finished-machine demand generates planned orders for machines, then requirements for boilers and pumps. Shortages of those assemblies generate their own planned orders and, in turn, dependent requirements for three purchased parts. Two parts are shared by both assemblies.

Teaching assumptions: one-day assembly lead time, one-day supplier lead time, lot-for-lot component planning, no safety stock, and supplier confirmations and shipping notices are modeled as explicit document stages; supplier lead times and delivery reliability are simplified.

Procurement execution

Purchase components

Turn MRP purchase proposals into supplier orders and record their arrival.

Run MRP to generate purchase requisitions for raw-material shortages.

A purchase requisition (PurRqs) is an internal proposal. A purchase order item (POitem) represents an order placed with a supplier. A shipping notification (ShpgNt) reports dispatch. Physical inventory increases only when goods receipt (GR) is posted.
Production execution

Manufacture espresso machines

Convert the manufacturing proposal, issue required components, and receive finished machines.

Run MRP to generate a production proposal.

Production order authorizes manufacturing. Goods issue (GI) consumes components. Goods receipt (GR) adds completed espresso machines to inventory.

SAP vocabulary · MRP element abbreviations

Use this reference to decode MD04. Hover over (or focus) an MRP Element in the Stock/Requirements List to see its meaning without leaving the table.

AbbreviationFull termWhat it means in the factory
StockStock on handPhysical inventory currently available for this material.
IndReqIndependent requirement (PIR)Forecast demand entered independently of component production; it may be consumed by sales orders under some planning strategies.
CustStCustomer stock requirementA customer-related requirement display; the precise meaning depends on SAP process and configuration.
OrderSales order requirementActual customer demand recorded through a sales order.
DepReqDependent requirementNeed for a component generated by planned production of its parent assembly.
ReserReservationComponents earmarked for a production order; a reservation is not yet a goods issue.
PldOrdPlanned orderMRP proposal to manufacture a quantity on a planned date; it is not yet an executable production order.
PrdOrdProduction orderManufacturing order used to authorize and track production execution.
PurRqsPurchase requisitionInternal proposal or request to buy a material; not yet an order to a supplier.
POitemPurchase order itemA line of a purchase order sent to a supplier for a specified quantity and delivery date.
ShpgNtShipping notificationNotice that a supplier has dispatched goods; physical stock has not yet been received.
GRGoods receiptPosting that records receipt of material and increases physical stock.
GIGoods issuePosting that records consumption or withdrawal of material and decreases physical stock.

MRP = Material Requirements Planning: calculating what is needed, how much, and when. MD04 = SAP Stock/Requirements List: a dated view of supply, demand, and projected available quantity. BOM = Bill of Materials: components and quantities needed to build a parent product. PIR = Planned Independent Requirement: forecast demand.

Lot-for-lot (L4L) sizing: An MRP lot-sizing rule that proposes a supply quantity equal to the uncovered net requirement for that planning period, rather than rounding up to a fixed batch size. For example, a shortage of 25 gaskets leads to a proposal for 25 gaskets. In CremaWorks, purchased components use lot-for-lot planning.

Effective demand (simulation term): The quantity MRP plans for after applying the selected demand strategy. Under Forecast consumption, a PIR of 50 and customer orders of 30 yield 50 units of demand because the orders consume part of the forecast. Under Separate, the same inputs yield 80 units because the requirements are added. Actual SAP behavior depends on planning strategy and consumption settings.

Planning vs. execution: PldOrd and PurRqs are proposals; PrdOrd and POitem are committed execution/procurement documents. GI and GR are physical inventory postings. A supplier shipping notification does not itself increase stock.

Terminology is simplified for teaching. Some SAP display labels vary by configuration and transaction context.

Educational approximation, not connected to SAP. Shortage replanning retains existing documents and proposes incremental purchases. Actual MD04 behavior depends on planning strategy, consumption settings, MRP type, procurement, scheduling, inventory status, and SAP configuration. The simulation uses relative days and assumes each production order is completed in full.

Production planning workflow

  1. Enter forecast demand (PIRs) and customer orders for ESP-100Forecasts and customer orders create requirements, not production orders. Depending on the demand strategy, orders may consume the forecast.
  2. Run MRPMRP calculates the shortage and, if necessary, generates a planned order (PldOrd).
  3. Convert planned order to production orderThis button becomes enabled only when MRP creates an unconverted ESP-100 planned order. A knowledge-check answer never enables it.
  4. Issue components and execute productionPhysical inventory changes when goods movements are posted.
Knowledge checks earn points but never change the factory. Planning creates proposals; execution changes physical stock. Purchased components may need to arrive before goods issue, but converting a planned order does not itself require a goods receipt.
